text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"The retrieved passages do not directly address older adults.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c2","text":"A systematic review and meta-analysis found body weight change was significantly greater after intermittent fasting than continuous calorie restriction in overweight and obese people.","cited_pids":["f5eeafdf6fc3#1"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"The same systematic review found no significant difference in BMI between intermittent fasting and continuous restriction.","cited_pids":["f5eeafdf6fc3#1"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"The systematic review searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane and Web of Science and performed sensitivity and publication-bias analyses.","cited_pids":["f5eeafdf6fc3#0"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"A trial in obese women found that intermittent fasting combined with calorie restriction produced weight loss.","cited_pids":["23334c40ad6b#0"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"A trial in obese people with type 2 diabetes found that 16:8 and 14:10 fasting produced greater percentage weight loss than control.","cited_pids":["201567a834f8#1"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"In the trial of obese people with type 2 diabetes, 16:8 fasting produced greater weight loss than 14:10 fasting.","cited_pids":["201567a834f8#1"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"A study in older adults on intermittent fasting addressed brain outcomes rather than weight.","cited_pids":["3bd31b026f03#2"]},{"cid":"c9","text":"Intermittent fasting may modestly outperform continuous calorie restriction for weight loss.","cited_pids":[]}]}
